content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge is resolving a collision between the defender's and challenger's read-together chains over the Acts 2:30 link, so K-C governs how that collision must be weighed.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' — one reading requires comparing the support/grounding of each whole chain; the other would allow deciding by whether a particular verse explicitly names the channel.", "why": "The judge leaves the point open because no cited text explicitly names whose body is the channel, which is the retired stating-verse approach rather than weighing the two chains by footing."}
